bullets.title: FOXA/ROKU: Fox acquires Roku for $160/sh ($22B EV); FOXA -14%, mixed Street reaction
bullets.body: Fox agreed to acquire Roku for $160/share ($96 cash + 0.9693 Class A shares), valuing Roku at ~$22B EV; Fox shareholders own ~73% pro forma, deal closes H1 2027. Combined company becomes third-largest US TV player with ~10% viewing share; ~$400M run-rate cost synergies, FCF/share accretive by year 2. FOXA hit 52-week low (-17.4% on day); Citi calls the ~14% FOXA drop an overreaction, maintains Buy/$78 PT; UBS values combined entity at 7.5x-8.5x 2027E EBITDA vs. DIS 9x/NFLX 16x. William Blair and Oppenheimer both downgraded ROKU to market perform/perform.

bullets.title: WDC/STX: MS raises PTs to $650/$1,035 on HDD pricing supercycle through CY28
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Erik Woodring raises WDC PT to $650 and STX PT to $1,035 after Asia checks show stronger nearline HDD pricing and supply shortages extending through CY28. Current HDD price is <$15/TB with vendors targeting $25-30/TB over 2-3 years; base case FY28 EPS is 70% above consensus with a bull case of 10x EPS growth CY25-CY28. WDC management guides EB supply growth +30-35% annually and customers signing LTAs through 2032; WDC HAMR (44TB) ahead on hyperscaler qualification. Both stocks hit 52-week highs on the day (WDC +15%, STX +7.9%).

bullets.title: INTC/MRVL/ALAB: MS semis bus tour bullish on AI interconnect shift
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's semis bus tour sees AI infrastructure value shifting toward interconnect, scale-up, optics, packaging, and memory — away from raw compute. INTC CEO Lip-Bu Tan doubling down on Foundry; 14A targeting 0.5 defect density with risk production 2028. MRVL custom silicon opportunity seen at $4B-$10B with connectivity at $10B growing ~70% Y/Y. ALAB reiterated OW with content per XPU already ~$1,000 and rising as systems become increasingly interconnect-intensive.

bullets.title: AMD/MU/SNDK: Memory/semi names surge to 52-week highs on AI demand
bullets.body: AMD hit a new 52-week high, up +8.0% on the day and +366% YTD. MU surged +7.9% pre-market on AI infrastructure demand; SNDK up +3.2% to 52-week high. Electronic Technology sector led all sectors with 33 new 52-week highs. Memory shortage is also boosting smartphone supply chain costs per Counterpoint research.

bullets.title: CRM: Acquires Fin for $3.6B; Agentforce ARR hits $1.2B, up 200%+ Y/Y
bullets.body: Salesforce is acquiring Fin (AI customer service agent) for $3.6B (~9x total ARR), closing Q4 FY27. Fin autonomously resolves 76% of support volume, has $100M ARR growing ~3.5x, and a 30,000+ customer base skewed SMB/mid-market. Wolfe maintains Outperform, seeing Fin as a 'plug and play' complement to Agentforce's 'build your own' approach; no change to FY27 guidance or capital return.

bullets.title: META: Tracking billions in internal AI spend; token limits and AI Gateway planned for 2027
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes META is tracking to spend billions on internal AI usage in 2026 and plans to implement token limits and an AI Gateway dashboard in 2027 to manage structured allocation. Token efficiency focus is rising broadly — Revolut achieved 8x cost savings and ElevenLabs achieved 70x throughput gains. META named as a top online ad pick by Citi into Cannes '26.

bullets.title: TSEM: Multi-year InP epiwafer deal signed; Mizuho sees mid-teens EPS by 2028 vs. Street $8.35
bullets.body: Tower Semiconductor signed a multi-year IQE InP epiwafer supply deal as SiPho demand explodes; Mizuho expects management to raise FY26 revenue/GM targets from prior $2.8B/$38% GM guidance. Mizuho sees TSEM reaching mid-teens EPS by 2028 vs. Street $8.35, calling 25x P/E reasonable for a high-growth foundry. TSEM was up 5.4% pre-market.

bullets.title: ORCL: IaaS growing 90%+ Y/Y; post-earnings -10% seen as buying opportunity by Mizuho
bullets.body: Oracle Q4 results were strong with IaaS growing 90%+ Y/Y and FY27 CapEx guidance of $90-95B in line with revised estimates. Mizuho views the stock's ~10% post-earnings decline as a buying opportunity, noting the data center buildout theme remains intact.

bullets.title: LYV: MS sets $200 PT; regulatory fears on resale caps and bot bans called overblown
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Cameron sets a $200 PT on LYV (19x EV/EBITDA, mid-2027) and calls regulatory headwinds from resale price caps, bot bans, and all-in pricing overblown. Primary ticketing modeled at MSD% CAGR; majority of LYV earnings come from venues and primary ticketing. SPOT signed a live entertainment festival livestream deal with LYV, beating out AAPL and AMZN.

bullets.title: RH: Q1 beat but Q2 guide misses; Estates launch mid-June seen as key H2 catalyst
bullets.body: RH reported Q1 revenue beat (+1.0%), EPS beat ($0.15), and gross margin 230bps above consensus, but Q2 guide of +0.5-2.5% revenue growth missed the +4.6% consensus. Management flagged a $75M revenue tailwind from backorders in H2 and expects material margin improvement. Citi raised PT to $166 (from $150), TD Cowen to $175; Street is split with avg PT $153.80 implying minimal upside at current valuation of 23.6x NTM P/E.

bullets.title: TXN: Citi raises PT to $345 from $280; top pick on 800V data center analog recovery
bullets.body: Citi reiterated Texas Instruments as a top pick and raised its PT to $345 from $280, citing stronger analog recovery driven by data center demand and the 800V DC transition. The 800V sidecar opportunity from NVDA-led deployments is expected late 2H27.

bullets.title: VST: Helix Digital platform seen adding $23/sh value; AI data center infra play
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley highlights that Vistra's investment in Helix Digital (a $10B infrastructure platform with KKR, NVDA, and KIA) offers $23/sh value potential. Helix targets mid-to-upper-teens unlevered returns for data center shell infrastructure with long-term contracts, and Vistra is positioned to accelerate power contracting for its existing fleet.

bullets.title: MDB: DA Davidson bullish on Early Access/vector search; 20%+ revenue growth expected
bullets.body: DA Davidson reiterates Buy on MongoDB, citing pent-up demand for vector search and Early Access programs as drivers of sustained 20%+ total revenue growth. Commentary came from their tech conference takeaways call.

bullets.title: ACN: Morgan Stanley downgrades to Equal Weight
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley downgraded Accenture to Equal Weight; ACN was -1% pre-market on the news. No specific PT or detailed thesis was included in the forwarded summary, but a follow-up Zoom call with management was scheduled by MS for June 15.

bullets.title: GOOGL: $1.5B Alabama data center investment; named Citi top ad pick into Cannes
bullets.body: Google announced a $1.5B investment in 2026-2027 to expand its Jackson County, Alabama data center campus, covering 100% of power costs and having contracted 300+ MW of new generation in the Tennessee Valley to date. Separately, Citi named GOOGL a top online ad pick heading into Cannes '26, with AI-monetization and agentic commerce as key themes.

bullets.title: DKNG: Hedgeye cautious; prediction market at $3.1B annualized but de-minimis P&L
bullets.body: Hedgeye cuts its outlook on DraftKings' prediction market business, noting annualized volume of $3.1B but characterizing the P&L impact as de-minimis, with DKNG significantly trailing competitor Kalshi on a monthly basis.

bullets.title: BKNG/EXPE: BofA sees both as top ME conflict resolution beneficiaries; BKNG down 3%, EXPE implied undervalued vs. TRIP
bullets.body: BofA reiterates Buy on Booking (down 3% since conflict start 2/27) on EU travel recovery post-World Cup. Separately, TRIP's TheFork sale at 17x '27 EBITDA implies TRIP's Experiences segment trades at 8.4x/'26 vs. EXPE at 10x and BKNG at 12x, suggesting ~$3.25/share upside if Experiences re-rates to EXPE-like multiples.

bullets.title: WBD/PSKY: DOJ approves Paramount-WBD $111B merger; state AG challenges remain
bullets.body: The DOJ approved the Paramount Skydance (PSKY) acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) in a deal valued at approximately $111B. MS notes the combined entity enables ~30 film releases and NFLX is separately exploring theatrical distribution. State attorneys general challenges remain a residual risk.

bullets.title: MSFT: CEO argues enterprise learning loops — not frontier models — capture AI value
bullets.body: Microsoft CEO's blog post argues AI value should accrue to enterprise-specific learning loops and sovereign company systems, not frontier model concentration. Separately, Rohan Kumar is joining Salesforce from Microsoft after 28 years to lead its Headless 360 and agentic enterprise business.

bullets.title: RDDT/PINS/APP: Citi's top small/mid ad picks into Cannes; ad pause post-ME conflict fading
bullets.body: Citi names RDDT, APP, and PINS among top online ad picks into Cannes '26 alongside large caps. BofA notes that online ad small caps (PINS, RDDT, SNAP) saw a pause in ad spending in March but guidance held stable, and large caps faced capex concern pressure; eCommerce remained least impacted throughout the Middle East conflict period.
